definitions.gloss: dejection; depression; being dispirited; low spirits
definitions.explanation: A state of having lost one's enthusiasm or motivation, feeling downcast or demoralized. A four-character compound expressing deep discouragement.

examples.japanese: チームは{意気消沈|いきしょうちん}していた。
{試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けて{意気消沈|いきしょうちん}する{選手|せんしゅ}たちを{励|はげ}ました。
examples.english: I encouraged the players who were dejected after losing the game.

examples.japanese: プロジェクトの{中止|ちゅうし}が{決|き}まり、{部署|ぶしょ}{全体|ぜんたい}が{意気消沈|いきしょうちん}してしまった。
examples.english: When the project cancellation was decided, the entire department became demoralized.

notes:
USAGE:
A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) used as a suru-verb ({意気消沈|いきしょうちん}する). The opposite expression is {意気揚々|いきようよう} (in high spirits, triumphant).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {意気消沈|いきしょうちん}する (to become dejected)
- {意気消沈|いきしょうちん}している (to be in low spirits)
- すっかり{意気消沈|いきしょうちん}する (to become completely dispirited)
